note: Friday 07:00 SGT sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Thu 23 Jul US close — levels/quotes are as of that close unless noted. The dominant cross-portfolio driver flipped this run: a Middle-East escalation (Houthi tanker strikes, collapsed ceasefire) sent Brent above $100 and triggered a risk-off US selloff led by mega-cap tech, with Treasury yields at year-highs into the 28-29 Jul FOMC. Fresh items (5 of 14) are dated 23 Jul; the rest are decision-relevant items from 3-22 Jul. Every item source-verified against the cited pages.

items.headline: Oil shock: Brent tops $100 after Houthi strikes on two Saudi tankers and a collapsed ceasefire
items.summary: Brent crude jumped ~6-7% to ~$100/bbl intraday (WTI ~$90, +5%) on Thu 23 July after Iran-backed Houthis attacked two Saudi tankers claiming a port blockade, following renewed US strikes on Iran and a collapsed ceasefire. Goldman warned oil could hit $120 if the Strait of Hormuz — which carries ~one-fifth of global crude — stays disrupted. The spike was the day's dominant market driver.
items.actionable: The single biggest cross-portfolio driver: bullish for the energy sleeve and Seatrium's offshore-order backdrop and a safe-haven tailwind for metals, but it revives the inflation impulse that keeps the Fed/MAS hawkish — a headwind for HK tech, rate-sensitive S-REITs and levered silver. Trade the de-escalation risk, not the individual legs.

items.headline: Silver holds ~$60 while gold slips ~2% to ~$4,060 as real yields bite into Fed week
items.summary: September silver futures held near $60/oz on Thu 23 July (roughly flat, ~+130% YTD) on the war/inflation-hedge bid and copper-led industrial strength, while gold fell ~2% to ~$4,056-4,075 — hit by higher real yields (10Y ~4.62%) despite the risk-off. Gold is still ~+70% YTD but BofA flags a 'death cross', elevated net-longs and worst-quarter-in-13-years warning signs into the FOMC.
items.actionable: The levered silver/miner book is riding a genuine rebound but into a hawkish-Fed catalyst and toppy positioning — treat strength as a place to trim leverage/harvest, not add, ahead of 28-29 July. Gold's real-yield sensitivity is the near-term warning; $58 silver is the line to hold above.

items.headline: Melt-up cracks: S&P -1.2%, Nasdaq -2.2% as Alphabet -7% and Tesla -14% lead tech down; yields hit year-highs
items.summary: US equities sold off hard on Thu 23 July — S&P 500 -1.21% to 7,408.30, Nasdaq -2.15% to 25,137.69, Dow -0.97% — as the oil spike pushed Treasury yields to year-highs (10Y ~4.62%, 2Y ~4.26%). Alphabet fell ~7% on AI-capex worry and Tesla ~14% on earnings, amplifying the growth-led decline. Longer-term breadth stayed broad (~69% of the S&P above its 200-DMA into the day).
items.actionable: A risk-off US tape and year-high yields are a negative read-through for HK-tech beta (SMIC 0981, the Tencent book) and rate-sensitive S-REITs. But credit is calm (HY ~268bp) and breadth broad, so this looks like a sharp oil/rate narrowing rather than a break — watch whether the 29 July FOMC deepens or resolves it.

items.headline: Singapore core inflation accelerates to 1.6% just before the end-July MAS review
items.summary: Singapore core CPI quickened to 1.6% (from prior) as higher global energy costs feed through, Bloomberg reported on 23 July, with the MAS policy review due before end-July. MAS already raised its 2026 core/headline forecast to 1.5-2.5% in April and steepened the SGD NEER appreciation path.
items.actionable: A hawkish MAS tilt pressures the S-REIT sleeve (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PAC, CapLand China Trust) via a stronger SGD and higher-for-longer bias; the MPS outcome is the near-term REIT catalyst. SGD strength is a mild drag on the USD cash pile's local purchasing power.

items.headline: Fed decision 28-29 July: ~83% hold priced, no cut, live hike tail under hawkish Chair Warsh
items.summary: CME FedWatch prices ~83% odds of no change at the 28-29 July FOMC, keeping the funds rate at 3.50-3.75%, with a cut off the table for July and a residual ~17-25% hike tail on the oil impulse. Chair Kevin Warsh has scrapped forward guidance for pure data-dependence and leans hawkish; June CPI cooled to 3.5% headline / 2.6% core but the late-July oil surge threatens re-acceleration.
items.actionable: A hawkish-hold or hike risk is the single biggest near-term threat to levered silver and S-REITs, keeping rates higher-for-longer. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder — keep it for a post-FOMC precious-metals shakeout; a dovish 29 July surprise is the upside catalyst.

items.headline: China's entity-specific rare-earth export ban on MP Materials & USA Rare Earth draws active July enforcement
items.summary: Beijing added 10 US entities including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its dual-use export-control list (immediate effect 22 June), and law firms note active July enforcement on rare earths/strategic minerals. MP fell ~13% on the June news; Lynas was not targeted and is advancing a US magnet-supply MOU with Noveon. The IEA has warned full curbs risk $6.5T of downstream production.
items.actionable: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist (Lynas, Energy Fuels, Iluka) and JL MAG's China-magnet position — a dip in MP on headlines is a watchlist entry, not an exit. The 10 Nov control-suspension expiry is the key catalyst to accumulate ex-China names on weakness.

items.headline: MP Materials' Pentagon + Apple deals recast the US magnet growth story with a $110/kg NdPr floor
items.summary: The US DoD holds a ~15% MP stake (~$400M preferred + warrants) with a 10-year, 7,000 t/yr magnet offtake at a $110/kg NdPr price floor; Apple added a $500M magnet/recycling partnership. A second US magnet plant ('10X' Texas) commissions from 2028, building out domestic vertical integration.
items.actionable: The $110/kg price floor de-risks the entire Western rare-earth complex on the watchlist — a policy tailwind that supports adding to ex-China miners on China-retaliation dips rather than chasing headlines.

items.headline: Tencent scales AI compute after Hunyuan-3 launch overloads systems; HK$5bn early-July buybacks
items.summary: Tencent had to rapidly scale compute after demand for its new Hunyuan-3 (Hy3) model, released 6 July, overloaded systems — the first major milestone under new chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu, claiming ~90% success on agent tasks across WeCom, Marvis and ima. Tencent also spent HK$5.01B on buybacks in early July.
items.actionable: Genuine AI-product traction plus aggressive buybacks underpin the Tencent thesis — the core HK-tech position to hold through China-tech volatility, and the relative-strength name to favor over Xiaomi in the trio.

items.headline: Singapore Q2 GDP beats at +5.7% as AI/electronics demand offsets the Iran-war drag
items.summary: Advance Q2 GDP grew 5.7% y/y (1.1% q/q), beating forecasts though cooling from Q1's revised 6.3%, buoyed by AI/electronics demand despite Middle-East headwinds. The print supports a resilient domestic backdrop into the SGX Q2 earnings season.
items.actionable: A resilient domestic economy supports DBS credit quality and the property/consumer names (UOL, CityDev, VICOM) into DBS's early-August earnings — a positive backdrop that partly offsets the hawkish-MAS S-REIT headwind.

items.headline: Seatrium doubles dividend and swings FCF positive with a ~S$32B deal pipeline
items.summary: Seatrium doubled its final dividend to S$0.03, swung free cash flow positive (+S$19.7M), holds a S$17.8B order book and is chasing >S$32B of oil & gas / offshore-wind / conversion work over 24 months; it also hit a wind-turbine-installation-vessel milestone with Maersk.
items.actionable: High oil and a swelling offshore order book make Seatrium the best direct energy-capex beneficiary in the SGX sleeve — the standout SGX momentum name, reporting H1 results around 24 July.

items.headline: Newmont Q2 on record gold prices spotlights the GDX-vs-spot lag
items.summary: Newmont, GDX's largest holding, reported/was due to report Q2 (consensus ~$1.98 non-GAAP EPS, ~$6.31B revenue) benefiting from much higher realized gold prices, partly offset by lower production and cost inflation. GDX traded ~$76.71 on 22 July, still -10.8% YTD — miners lagging the metal.
items.actionable: Miner margins should expand on record gold, but GDX's YTD lag vs spot signals cost inflation is capping equity upside — favor the metal and SLVP quality over broad GDX beta.

items.headline: US-China chip framework: H200 sales resume under caps as SMIC pushes 5nm pilot runs
items.summary: Under the current framework, Nvidia H200 sales to China are licensed with a 50% volume cap, third-party security testing and a 25% chip tariff. SMIC doubled 2026 7nm capacity plans, took full control of its Beijing fab ($5.79B) and entered 5nm pilot runs (DUV multi-patterning) for Huawei/Alibaba.
items.actionable: Restricted US chip access accelerates China's domestic-fab reliance — a structural tailwind for SMIC despite equipment constraints; hold on the decoupling-driven localization thesis.

items.headline: Xiaomi cuts jobs on a sharp profit decline, lagging the HK-tech trio
items.summary: Xiaomi began layoffs across multiple units amid a sharp profit drop; it and SMIC were among names down 2.5-3% in a recent HK-tech pullback, though Xiaomi also ran buybacks. EV-cost drag continues to weigh on margins.
items.actionable: Deteriorating Xiaomi margins make it the weakest link in the HK-tech trio — consider rotating weight toward Tencent on relative strength (AI traction + buybacks) while the EV-investment drag runs.

items.headline: Bitcoin rangebound ~$66k, Ether ~$1,900 as the bottom debate drags on
items.summary: Bitcoin opened ~$66,081 (-0.6%) on 23 July, trading ~$65,659; Ether ~$1,933 easing toward ~$1,899. BTC is boxed $64k-$66.8k after a 13% bounce off July lows, with macro giving little direction. Crypto Fear & Greed sits at 31 (Fear).
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto's listless, rangebound tape confirms muted risk appetite — no 'risk-on' confirmation for HK-tech longs; treat as a neutral barometer. A sustained hold above ~$66k is constructive, a break under ~$64k the early risk-off tell.
